---
title: "Stats 101A Group Project — Predicting NFL Wins from Team Ranking Stats"
author: "Jeremy Shiu"
date: "2023-03-19"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

<!--
  Goal: model regular-season WINS as a function of five team ranking
  statistics (lower rank number = better):
    rypa        rushing yards per attempt (offense) ranking
    yppa        passing yards per attempt (offense) ranking
    t.o_margin  turnover margin ranking
    oppo.rypa   opponent rushing yards per attempt (defense) ranking
    oppo.yppa   opponent passing yards per attempt (defense) ranking
-->

## 1. Setup

```{r libraries, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(car)   # inverseResponsePlot, powerTransform, avPlot, vif
library(MASS)  # supporting model-selection utilities
```

## 2. Load and prepare the data

```{r load-data}
# Read the raw rankings file (column 1 is the team label; columns 2-7 are numeric).
football_raw <- read.csv("football data.csv")

# Row 104 is the winless 2017 Browns (wins = 0). It is an outlier and its zero
# breaks the log / power transformations used later, so it is dropped.
# Keep only the numeric response + predictor columns (2-7).
football <- football_raw[-104, 2:7]

# Number of observations, used later for the BIC penalty term.
n <- nrow(football)

head(football)
```

## 3. Exploratory data analysis

```{r eda}
# Summary statistics and spread for each variable.
summary(football)
list("std. devs" = sapply(football, sd))

# Correlations and scatterplot matrix among all variables.
cor(football)
pairs(football)
```

## 4. Full model

```{r full-model}
# Regress wins on all five ranking predictors.
full_model <- lm(wins ~ rypa + yppa + t.o_margin + oppo.rypa + oppo.yppa,
                 data = football)
summary(full_model)
anova(full_model)

# Standard diagnostic plots (residuals, Q-Q, scale-location, leverage).
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(full_model)
```

```{r leverage}
# Flag high-leverage points using the 2*(p+1)/n rule of thumb.
# p = 5 predictors, so the cutoff is 2*(5+1)/n.
which(hatvalues(full_model) > 2 * (5 + 1) / n)
```

## 5. Choosing a response transformation

```{r inverse-response-plot}
# The inverse response plot suggests a power transformation of the response.
inverseResponsePlot(full_model)
```

```{r power-transform}
# powerTransform estimates transformation parameters for the response
# (and, below, jointly for the predictors) via maximum likelihood.
summary(
  powerTransform(
    cbind(wins, rypa, yppa, t.o_margin, oppo.rypa, oppo.yppa) ~ 1,
    data = football
  )
)

# The inverse response plot returns lambda ~ 0.8425 for wins; store it so the
# transformed response is defined in one place.
lambda <- 0.8425031
football$wins_t <- football$wins^lambda
```

## 6. Transformed full model

```{r transformed-model}
# Refit the full model using the transformed response.
trans_model <- lm(wins_t ~ rypa + yppa + t.o_margin + oppo.rypa + oppo.yppa,
                  data = football)
summary(trans_model)
anova(trans_model)

# Diagnostics for the transformed model.
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(trans_model)

# Re-check leverage and multicollinearity (VIF) after transforming.
which(hatvalues(trans_model) > 2 * (5 + 1) / n)
vif(trans_model)
```

## 7. Automated model selection

```{r stepwise-selection}
# Intercept-only starting point for forward selection.
null_model <- lm(wins_t ~ 1, data = football)
scope_upper <- ~ rypa + yppa + t.o_margin + oppo.rypa + oppo.yppa

# Forward and backward selection by AIC.
forward_aic  <- step(null_model, scope = list(lower = ~1, upper = scope_upper),
                     direction = "forward", data = football)
backward_aic <- step(trans_model, direction = "backward", data = football)

# Forward and backward selection by BIC (heavier penalty: k = log(n)).
forward_bic  <- step(null_model, scope = list(lower = ~1, upper = scope_upper),
                     direction = "forward", k = log(n), data = football)
backward_bic <- step(trans_model, direction = "backward", k = log(n),
                     data = football)
```

## 8. Added-variable plots and multicollinearity (full model)

```{r av-plots-full}
# Added-variable (partial regression) plots show each predictor's unique
# contribution given the others; VIF quantifies multicollinearity.
par(mfrow = c(3, 3))
avPlot(trans_model, variable = rypa,       ask = FALSE)
avPlot(trans_model, variable = yppa,       ask = FALSE)
avPlot(trans_model, variable = t.o_margin, ask = FALSE)
avPlot(trans_model, variable = oppo.rypa,  ask = FALSE)
avPlot(trans_model, variable = oppo.yppa,  ask = FALSE)
vif(trans_model)
```

## 9. Reduced model and partial F-test

```{r reduced-model}
# Model selection points to the three consistently significant predictors:
# turnover margin, passing offense, and passing defense.
reduced_model <- lm(wins_t ~ t.o_margin + yppa + oppo.yppa, data = football)

# Partial F-test: does dropping rypa and oppo.rypa significantly hurt fit?
# A non-significant p-value supports the smaller model.
anova(reduced_model, trans_model)
```

```{r av-plots-reduced}
# Added-variable plots and VIF for the reduced model.
par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
avPlot(reduced_model, variable = t.o_margin, ask = FALSE)
avPlot(reduced_model, variable = yppa,       ask = FALSE)
avPlot(reduced_model, variable = oppo.yppa,  ask = FALSE)
vif(reduced_model)
```

## 10. Final reduced model diagnostics

```{r final-diagnostics}
# Summary, ANOVA, and diagnostic plots for the final chosen model.
summary(reduced_model)
anova(reduced_model)
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(reduced_model)
```
